title: Origins and History of Mauser Gewehr 98
body:
The Mauser Gewehr 98 belongs to the 1898–1945 era and traces to Mauser.

The torsion catapult and ballista armed Rome; the trebuchet (12th c.) perfected gravity artillery, throwing 150-kg stones at castles. The longbow (Crécy, 1346; Agincourt, 1415) ended the armored knight's dominance; gunpowder (China, then Europe by 1300s) replaced them all. Matchlocks (1400s), wheellocks, then flintlocks (1600s) armed musketeers; the socket bayonet (1700s) made pikemen obsolete. Smoothbore cannon — bronze then iron — sieged and ship-fought for 400 years; rifling and the Minié ball (1840s) made the Civil War rifle-musket lethal at 500 yards. Smokeless powder (1880s) ended this era.

Within that longer story, Mauser Gewehr 98: The 1898; the 9M. The 98 is the bolt's standard.

title: How Mauser Gewehr 98 Works
body:
Torsion engines twist sinew/hair skeins to store energy; the trebuchet drops a counterweight to whip a sling. Bows store energy in bending limbs; the crossbow's spanning mechanisms (cranequin, windlass) multiply the soldier's strength. Matchlocks lower a burning cord to a priming pan; wheellocks spin serrated steel against pyrite; flintlocks strike flint on steel, showering sparks. Smoothbore muskets fire round balls with windage; rifling spins the Minié ball for accuracy. Black powder (saltpeter/charcoal/sulfur) burns fast and smoky — the white battlefield cloud.

Applied to the Mauser Gewehr 98 (1898–1945, Mauser): The 98 is the bolt's standard.

The engineering principles above are exactly what made this class of technology practical: every unit is a working compromise between materials, energy, precision, and cost.

title: Mauser Gewehr 98 — Trebuchet range physics (Runnable Python)
body:
Estimates trebuchet projectile range from counterweight energy — the siege engineer's physics, demonstrated safely as mathematics.

The program below is real, runnable Python 3. Save it as demo.py and run `python3 demo.py`. It models the core mathematics of the Mauser Gewehr 98 so you can experiment with the parameters yourself.
code:
# Trebuchet physics (public-domain mechanics; math demonstration only)
import math

def trebuchet_range(counterweight_kg, drop_m, projectile_kg, efficiency=0.35):
    # energy = m*g*h * efficiency -> projectile velocity -> range at 45deg
    e = counterweight_kg * 9.81 * drop_m * efficiency
    v = math.sqrt(2 * e / projectile_kg)
    return v**2 / 9.81  # 45-degree range

r = trebuchet_range(6000, 8, 50)
print(f"6-ton counterweight, 8m drop, 50kg stone: ~{r:.0f} m range")
print("(Warwolf-class engines reportedly threw 140kg+ stones hundreds of meters)")
# Longbow energy for comparison
print(f"\nlongbow (~150 lbf draw, 30in): ~{150*4.448*0.762/2:.0f} J stored (approx)")
